### Description

Videos cannot be played on Linux when video `source` element `src` attribute contains wails url (or relative url because it converts to absolute wails url).

items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

# Feature Request: Cross-Platform Network Request Interception (WebView2, WKWebView, WebKitGTK)

## 💡 Summary
Currently, Wails v3 does not expose native web engine network interception APIs.  
It would be very useful if Wails could support request interception across all supported platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux).

## 🚀 Feature Request
Please consider adding an API (or event hook) in Wails to enable network request interception.

Example Go-level API:
```go
app.OnWebRequest(pattern string, handler func(req *WebRequest) *WebResponse)
```

### Possible internal mappings:
| Platform | Engine | Native API |
|-----------|---------|------------|
| Windows | Edge WebView2 | `ICoreWebView2::AddWebResourceRequestedFilter()` + `WebResourceRequested` |
| macOS | WKWebView | `WKURLSchemeHandler` / `decidePolicyForNavigationAction` |
| Linux | WebKitGTK | `WebKitURISchemeRequest` / `resource-load-started` |

## 🧩 Motivation / Use Cases
1. **Security:** Block or sanitize requests to untrusted domains.  
2. **Local Resource Replacement:** Serve static or offline resources from Go memory or local files.  
3. **Request Logging:** Audit or monitor outgoing network traffic from the frontend.  
4. **Offline Mode:** Intercept requests and respond from cache when offline.  
5. **Testing:** Mock or stub backend responses without modifying frontend code.  

## ⚙️ Current Workarounds
- Hook `fetch()` / `XMLHttpRequest` in JavaScript (works only for API calls, not static assets).  
- Use a Service Worker (limited to browser context, no control over all resource types).  
- Run a local proxy server (heavy and indirect).  

None of these offer full parity with the native web engines’ interception capabilities.

## 🖥️ Platform Details

### 🪟 Windows (Edge WebView2)
WebView2 supports complete interception via:
```cpp
ICoreWebView2::AddWebResourceRequestedFilter(L"*", COREWEBVIEW2_WEB_RESOURCE_CONTEXT_ALL);
ICoreWebView2::add_WebResourceRequested(handler);
```
Developers can fully inspect, modify, or block requests.

### 🍎 macOS (WKWebView)
Supports interception via:
- `WKURLSchemeHandler` — for custom protocols like `local://`
- `decidePolicyForNavigationAction` — to allow or block requests dynamically

### 🐧 Linux (WebKitGTK)
Supports interception via:
- `webkit_web_context_register_uri_scheme()` to handle custom schemes
- `"resource-load-started"` signal to observe or cancel requests

## 🙏 Why This Matters
All three engines (WebView2, WKWebView, WebKitGTK) natively support request interception.  
Wails currently does not expose this layer, limiting developers who need to control, audit, or simulate network traffic.  

Exposing this feature would give developers parity with Electron’s `webRequest.onBeforeRequest` API and enable building:
- security-sensitive desktop applications  
- offline-first or embedded data apps  
- developer tools with full network visibility  

## 🔧 References
- [Microsoft Docs – WebResourceRequested](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/reference/win32/icorewebview2?view=webview2-1.0.2478.35#webresourcerequested)
- [Apple Docs – WKURLSchemeHandler](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/webkit/wkurlschemehandler)
- [WebKitGTK Docs – WebKitURISchemeRequest](https://webkitgtk.org/reference/webkit2gtk/stable/WebKitURISchemeRequest.html)

---

> A unified Go-level API like `runtime.OnWebRequest` could internally map to:
> - WebView2 → `WebResourceRequested`
> - WKWebView → `WKURLSchemeHandler`
> - WebKitGTK → `WebKitURISchemeRequest`
>
> I would be happy to help test or contribute a PR for this functionality.


### Describe the solution you'd like

🧠 Describe Alternatives You've Considered

Currently, there are several partial workarounds, but none provide full control:

Hooking fetch() or XMLHttpRequest in JavaScript – works only for API requests, not for static resources (images, CSS, etc.).

Using a Service Worker – can intercept some requests, but limited to browser context and not all protocols.

Running a local HTTP proxy – possible but adds unnecessary complexity, extra configuration, and dependency.

Embedding a custom HTTP server inside Wails – can reroute frontend requests through Go, but cannot intercept assets requested directly by the WebView engine.

None of these approaches provide true native-level interception like WebResourceRequested, WKURLSchemeHandler, or WebKitURISchemeRequest.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

items.title: Closing The Terminal while running "wails3 dev" does not kill process "MainThread"
items.body: ### Wails version family v3 ### Exact Wails version v3.0.0-beta.27 ### Operating System Linux ### Description When closing the terminal while ```wails3 dev``` is running the program does not shutdown, and instead continues running. Closing the program works, but when I open a new shell and run ```wails3 dev``` I get error: **ERROR listen tcp 127.0.0.1:9245: bind: address already in use** From what I found this is caused by ```wails3 dev``` not killing a process called **MainThread**. which also causes the port to still be in use. The only way to fix this that I found is to run ```pkill MainThread``` ### To Reproduce 1. Run ```wails3 dev``` 2. Close the shell 3. Open a new shell 4. Run ```wails3 dev```, you should get the error ### Expected behaviour Closing the shell should kill the entire program and not leave a process that causes ```wails3 dev``` to fail ### Screenshots This is after reproducing the bug this is what I found from running ```sudo netstat -tulnp``` ### Attempted Fixes _No response_ ### System Details ```shell Wails v3.0.0-beta.27 › Wails Doctor # items.title: GTK4: frameless window resize jumps wildly — widget-local coords passed to gdk_toplevel_begin_resize which expects root coords
items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.28

### Operating System

Linux

### Description

On Linux with the GTK4 backend, resizing a frameless window from any corner/edge makes the window instantly jump and stretch (often beyond the screen). The resize gesture is completely unusable.
Environment:
- Wails v3.0.0-beta.28
- Linux, GTK4 backend (default build, no extra tags)
- WebviewWindowOptions: Frameless: true
- Observed on Wayland and X11

### To Reproduce

`handleButtonPressed` in `pkg/application/linux_cgo.go` (~line 1698) stores the
GtkGesture click callback's **widget-local coordinates** into the drag state:

```go
lw.drag.XRoot = int(x)   // x is GtkGesture "pressed" signal coord — RELATIVE to the widget
lw.drag.YRoot = int(y)
lw.drag.DragTime = uint32(C.GDK_CURRENT_TIME)
```

`startResize` then forwards these as the pointer position to
`gdk_toplevel_begin_resize`, whose `x`/`y` parameters are documented as the
pointer's **root (screen) coordinates**:

```go
C.beginWindowResize(w.gtkWindow(), edge, ..., C.double(w.drag.XRoot), C.double(w.drag.YRoot), ...)
```

The resulting geometry anchor is off by the window's own position, so the WM
resizes relative to a wrong pointer location — the window teleports/stretches.
`GDK_CURRENT_TIME` (0) as the timestamp is also suspect on Wayland.

Notably the GTK3 backend does this correctly
(`pkg/application/linux_cgo_gtk3.go` ~line 2044 uses the event's real
`event.x_root`/`event.y_root`), which is why `gtk3`-tagged builds resize fine.

### Expected behaviour

Translate the gesture coordinates to root coordinates before storing them
(e.g. `gdk_surface_translate_coordinates`, or query the pointer position from
the seat at event time), and use the gesture event's timestamp instead of
`GDK_CURRENT_TIME`.

### Wails version family

v3

### Operating System

Windows

### Description

With `EnableFileDrop: true` and a `data-file-drop-target` element, dragging files over the window adds the `file-drop-target-active` class for hover styling. On **Windows**, if the user drags the files back out of the window (or cancels with Esc) instead of dropping, the class is never removed - any hover styling (e.g. the full-window overlay from the [File Drop docs](https://v3.wails.io/features/drag-and-drop/files/#full-window-drop)) stays visible indefinitely.

### To Reproduce

1. Minimal v3 app with `EnableFileDrop: true` and `<body data-file-drop-target>`.
2. Add the docs' hover CSS: `body.file-drop-target-active { outline: 4px dashed blue; }`.
3. Drag a file from Explorer over the window (outline appears).
4. Drag it back out of the window and release on the desktop.

### Expected behaviour

**Expected:** hover styling is removed when the drag leaves the window.
**Actual:** `file-drop-target-active` remains on `<body>` until a later drop occurs.

### Additional context

The runtime's document-level `dragleave` handler discards events whose
`relatedTarget` is `null`:

https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/master/v3/internal/runtime/desktop/%40wailsio/runtime/src/window.ts#L783-L787

```ts
// On Linux/WebKitGTK and macOS, dragleave fires immediately with relatedTarget=null when native
// drag handling is involved. Ignore these spurious events - we'll clean up on drop instead.
if (event.relatedTarget === null) {
    return;
}
```

Suggested fix
Make the null-relatedTarget early-return platform-aware: only skip these events on macOS/Linux (where hover is driven natively via handleDragEnter/Over/Leave anyway), and on Windows treat relatedTarget === null as leaving the window - remove the active class, reset dragEnterCounter, and clear currentDropTarget.

items.title: v2.14.0: multipart/form-data request body SIGSEGVs the Linux asset server (webkit2_41) and arrives empty on macOS
items.body:
### Description

Sending a `multipart/form-data` request body from the webview to a handler
mounted as `assetserver.Options{Handler: …}` behaves differently on each
platform in Wails v2.14.0:

- **Linux** (`-tags webkit2_41`, WebKitGTK 4.1): the process dies with `SIGSEGV`
  inside `webkit_uri_scheme_request_get_http_body`.
- **macOS** (WKWebView): the request reaches the handler with the right
  `Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=…`, but the body is empty —
  `r.MultipartReader()` gives `NextPart: EOF` after 0 bytes.
- **Windows** (WebView2): works correctly.

The same handler and the same payload sent as a raw `application/octet-stream`
or `text/plain` body arrive whole on all three platforms, at both 32 bytes and
2 MiB — so this is about the *shape* of the body rather than its size.

We hit this while measuring which asset-server transport primitives we could
build on. Linux desktop is not a target for us, so it isn't blocking our work;
we're reporting it because the crash takes the whole process down and seemed
worth having on record. Thanks for Wails — the rest of the asset server behaved
exactly as documented.

### Versions

| | |
|---|---|
| Wails | v2.14.0 |
| Go | 1.27.1 (`runtime.Version()` in the built binary) |
| Linux | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-1022-azure, x86_64 (GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest`) |
| Linux WebKitGTK | `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0` / `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` `2.52.6-0ubuntu0.24.04.1` |
| Linux build | `wails build -clean -skipbindings -tags webkit2_41` |
| Linux run | under `xvfb-run -a --server-args="-screen 0 1280x1024x24"` + `dbus-run-session`, with `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1` and `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1` |
| macOS | macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), arm64; `wails build -clean -skipbindings` |
| Windows (works) | Windows Server 2025 10.0.26100.33296, AMD64; WebView2 / Chromium 151 |

### To reproduce

The excerpts below are taken from our probe rig. It lives in a private
repository, so the relevant parts are inlined here rather than linked.

Mount an ordinary `http.Handler` as the asset server's `Handler`:

```go
err = wails.Run(&options.App{
    Title:  "transport spike",
    Width:  900,
    Height: 700,
    AssetServer: &assetserver.Options{
        Assets:  frontend, // embed.FS sub-FS holding index.html
        Handler: mux,
    },
})
```

Give the mux a handler that reads the request body as multipart:

```go
mux.HandleFunc("/probe/multipart", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    res := map[string]any{
        "method":         r.Method,
        "content_type":   r.Header.Get("Content-Type"),
        "content_length": r.Header.Get("Content-Length"),
    }
    mr, err := r.MultipartReader()
    if err != nil {
        res["parse_error"] = "MultipartReader: " + err.Error()
    } else {
        n := 0
        for {
            part, err := mr.NextPart()
            if err == io.EOF {
                break
            }
            if err != nil {
                res["parse_error"] = "NextPart: " + err.Error()
                break
            }
            b, _ := io.ReadAll(part)
            n += len(b)
        }
        res["bytes"] = n
    }
    json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(res)
})
```

From the page loaded in the webview, POST a `FormData` body. This 32-byte
version is enough — the payload size makes no difference:

```js
const fd = new FormData();
fd.append('file', new Blob([new Uint8Array(32)]), 'small.bin');
const r = await fetch('/probe/multipart?tag=small', { method: 'POST', body: fd });
const j = await r.json();
```

A ~2 MiB version behaves identically (crash on Linux, 0 bytes on macOS):

```js
const bytes = new Uint8Array(2 * 1024 * 1024);
const fd = new FormData();
fd.append('note', 'spike');
fd.append('file', new Blob([bytes], { type: 'application/octet-stream' }), 'payload.bin');
await fetch('/probe/multipart?tag=main', { method: 'POST', body: fd });
```

### Linux: stack trace

Verbatim from the CI log of the run that first surfaced it:

```
SIGSEGV: segmentation violation
PC=0x7fe561b53e5e m=8 sigcode=1 addr=0x28
signal arrived during cgo execution

goroutine 25 gp=0x2469f42b54a0 m=8 mp=0x2469f4296808 [syscall]:
runtime.cgocall(0x8f6ab0, 0x2469f427bcb8)
	/home/runner/go/pkg/mod/golang.org/toolchain@v0.0.1-go1.27.1.linux-amd64/src/runtime/cgocall.go:167 +0x4b fp=0x2469f427bc90 sp=0x2469f427bc58 pc=0x49154b
github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/pkg/assetserver/webview._Cfunc_webkit_uri_scheme_request_get_http_body(0x29d83430)
	_cgo_gotypes.go:437 +0x45 fp=0x2469f427bcb8 sp=0x2469f427bc90 pc=0x817685
github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/pkg/assetserver/webview.webkit_uri_scheme_request_get_http_body.func1(...)
	/home/runner/go/pkg/mod/github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2@v2.14.0/pkg/assetserver/webview/webkit2_40+.go:24
github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/pkg/assetserver/webview.webkit_uri_scheme_request_get_http_body(0x29d83430)
	/home/runner/go/pkg/mod/github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2@v2.14.0/pkg/assetserver/webview/webkit2_40+.go:24 +0x39 fp=0x2469f427bcf0 sp=0x2469f427bcb8 pc=0x819139
github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/pkg/assetserver/webview.(*request).Body(0x2469f43cf200)
	/home/runner/go/pkg/mod/github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2@v2.14.0/pkg/assetserver/webview/request_linux.go:63 +0x25 fp=0x2469f427bd08 sp=0x2469f427bcf0 pc=0x817de5
github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/pkg/assetserver.(*AssetServer).processWebViewRequestInternal(0x2469f42be140, {0xe64af0, 0x2469f4326918})
	/home/runner/go/pkg/mod/github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2@v2.14.0/pkg/assetserver/assetserver_webview.go:98 +0x4ac fp=0x2469f427bf60 sp=0x2469f427bd08 pc=0x83f94c
github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/pkg/assetserver.(*AssetServer).processWebViewRequest(0x2469f42be140, {0xe64af0, 0x2469f4326918})
	/home/runner/go/pkg/mod/github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2@v2.14.0/pkg/assetserver/assetserver_webview.go:57 +0x48 fp=0x2469f427bfb8 sp=0x2469f427bf60 pc=0x83f388
github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/pkg/assetserver.(*AssetServer).ServeWebViewRequest.gowrap1()
	/home/runner/go/pkg/mod/github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2@v2.14.0/pkg/assetserver/assetserver_webview.go:49 +0x1f fp=0x2469f427bfe0 sp=0x2469f427bfb8 pc=0x841d7f
runtime.goexit({})
	/home/runner/go/pkg/mod/golang.org/toolchain@v0.0.1-go1.27.1.linux-amd64/src/runtime/asm_amd64.s:1264 +0x1 fp=0x2469f427bfe8 sp=0x2469f427bfe0 pc=0x49b3e1
created by github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/pkg/assetserver.(*AssetServer).ServeWebViewRequest in goroutine 10
	/home/runner/go/pkg/mod/github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2@v2.14.0/pkg/assetserver/assetserver_webview.go:49 +0xe5
```

The lines immediately preceding it, in case they matter:

```
(maos-transport-spike:10151): dbind-WARNING **: 06:46:26.915: AT-SPI: Error retrieving accessibility bus address: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.ServiceUnknown: The name org.a11y.Bus was not provided by any .service files
Overriding existing handler for signal 10. Set JSC_SIGNAL_FOR_GC if you want WebKit to use a different signal
libEGL warning: DRI3 error: Could not get DRI3 device
libEGL warning: Ensure your X server supports DRI3 to get accelerated rendering
```

The crash reproduced on every run that sent a `FormData` body — the ~2 MiB
upload and the 32-byte one, each in its own process — with the same stack. Runs
of the same binary that sent a 2 MiB `text/plain` body or a 2 MiB
`application/octet-stream` body instead exited 0.

### macOS: the same request arrives with an empty body

No crash; the handler is reached and reports:

```
Content-Type:   multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundaryQ47DLnq2iyHcBW8V
Content-Length: (header absent)
bytes:          0
parse_error:    NextPart: multipart: NextPart: EOF
```

Identical at 32 bytes and at 2 MiB.

### What does work, on all three platforms

| Body | macOS | Windows | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` + 45-byte `application/json` | ok | ok | ok |
| `POST` + 2 MiB `text/plain` string | ok | ok | ok |
| `POST` + 2 MiB `application/octet-stream` (`Uint8Array`) | ok | ok | ok |
| `POST` + `multipart/form-data`, 32 B | 0 bytes | ok | SIGSEGV |
| `POST` + `multipart/form-data`, 2 MiB | 0 bytes | ok | SIGSEGV |

The 2 MiB binary body arrived byte-for-byte on all three (sha256
`1e075c8d478ad21844e33e830a695ef03a4d2488b69ee275bd8947618bb1be1e`).

One incidental observation while measuring the above: the `Content-Length`
header was empty on every request body on every platform, including bodies that
arrived whole.

### A note on the `webkit2_legacy` fallback

Building without `-tags webkit2_36|40|41` avoids the crash, but that path has no
request-body support at all — `webkit_uri_scheme_request_get_http_body` returns
`http.NoBody` unconditionally:

```go
// pkg/assetserver/webview/webkit2_legacy.go:35
func webkit_uri_scheme_request_get_http_body(_ *C.WebKitURISchemeRequest) io.ReadCloser {
	return http.NoBody
}
```

So on Linux in v2.14.0 the choice appears to be "request bodies work, but a
`FormData` body ends the process" or "request bodies are silently always empty".
Mentioning it in case it's useful for deciding where a fix belongs.

### Workaround we adopted

POST the raw bytes with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` and carry the
filename and any metadata in the URL or in request headers. That is measured
working at 2 MiB on all three platforms.

items.title: [v2] wailsjs file modes differ between `wails generate module` and `wails build`/`wails dev` — spurious git mode changes
items.body:
### Description

The same generated files get different permission bits depending on which command ran last:

- `wails generate module` → everything under `wailsjs/` becomes **0755** (including `.js`, `.d.ts`, `.json`)
- `wails build` / `wails dev` → `wailsjs/runtime/*` ends up **0644**, while `wailsjs/go/*` stays 0755

For projects that commit `wailsjs` (the shipped templates include it), this produces diffs with a mode change and zero content change, in both directions:

```
mode change 100644 => 100755  frontend/wailsjs/runtime/runtime.js   (after `wails generate module`)
mode change 100755 => 100644  frontend/wailsjs/runtime/runtime.js   (after `wails build`)
```

So no committed mode satisfies both commands — whichever one you commit, the other dirties the tree. The files are byte-identical; Windows is unaffected (git does not track the exec bit there).

Root cause, as far as I can trace it: two paths extract `wailsjs/runtime/`, and only the first is followed by a permission fixup.

- **Binding generation** — `v2/internal/app/app_bindings.go#L104-L123`: remove + gosod extract + `fs.SetPermissions(wailsjsbasedir, 0755)`. `fs.SetPermissions` (`v2/internal/fs/fs.go#L272-L279`) is `filepath.Walk` + `os.Chmod` without distinguishing files from directories, so regular files get the exec bit too. That comes from #1763 — not arguing it is wrong, just identifying the source of 0755.
- **Build / dev** — `generateRuntimeWrapper` (`v2/pkg/commands/build/base.go#L428-L445`, called at `#L158` from `CompileProject`): remove + gosod extract, which writes via `os.Create` → 0644, and nothing re-applies 0755 afterwards. It runs *after* the chmod above, which is why only `runtime/` flips back to 0644.

That also decides the fix, and it's your call:

- **0755 canonical** (per #1763) → apply the same permission step after `generateRuntimeWrapper`, or drop the redundant re-extract.
- **0644 canonical** → change `SetPermissions` so it only fixes up directories.

Happy to send a PR for either direction.

### To Reproduce

```bash
wails init -n modecheck -t vanilla-ts && cd modecheck

stat -c '%a  %n' frontend/wailsjs/runtime/* frontend/wailsjs/go/main/*   # all 644
wails generate module -tags webkit2_41
stat -c '%a  %n' frontend/wailsjs/runtime/* frontend/wailsjs/go/main/*   # all 755
wails build -s -tags webkit2_41
stat -c '%a  %n' frontend/wailsjs/runtime/* frontend/wailsjs/go/main/*   # runtime 644, go 755
wails generate module -tags webkit2_41
# runtime/* 755 again — flipping on every alternation
```

| step | `wailsjs/runtime/*` | `wailsjs/go/*` |
|---|---|---|
| `wails init` | 644 | 644 |
| `wails generate module` | 755 | 755 |
| `wails build` / `wails dev` | **644** | 755 |
| `wails generate module` again | **755** | 755 |

Note the first row: `wails init` writes everything 0644, so the very first `wails generate module` already turns a clean tree into five `mode change 100644 => 100755` entries.

### Expected behaviour

Both entry points leave the same permissions, so regenerating bindings is a no-op on a clean tree.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

- Searched the issue tracker, PRs and discussions for an existing report — no duplicate found.
- Traced both code paths myself and confirmed the ordering with a minimal `wails init` project (no git needed, just `stat`).
- Local workaround only: `git config --local core.fileMode false` — hides the diffs, does not fix the inconsistency.
- Considered sending a patch directly, but the intended direction (unify on 0755 vs 0644) is ambiguous because #1763 added the 0755 fixup deliberately, hence this ticket first.

### System Details


### Additional context

- Related but distinct: #2367 (runtime dir rewritten on every dev build), #2372 (closed attempt to stop rewriting it).
- `wails build` is what I ran; `wails dev` was not run (it starts a GUI), but it goes through the same `build.Build` path.
- The `libwebkit: Not Found` warning is the webkitgtk 4.0 vs 4.1 mismatch — this box only has webkit2gtk-4.1 (2.52.6), and builds were made with `-tags webkit2_41` and succeed.

items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Operating System

Android (experimental)

### Description

I encountered a bug where I would get a crash when minimizing the my App on Android:

```
07-31 16:24:43.096 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: WebView.destroy() called while WebView is still attached to window.
07-31 16:24:43.100 10758 10758 W WindowOnBackDispatcher: sendCancelIfRunning: isInProgress=false callback=android.view.ViewRootImpl$$ExternalSyntheticLambda14@d9795ca
07-31 16:24:43.105 10758 10758 D ViewRootImpl: Skipping stats log for color mode
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: Application attempted to call on a destroyed WebView
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: java.lang.Throwable
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: 	at org.chromium.android_webview.AwContents.p(chromium-SystemWebViewGoogle6432.aab-stable-787112403:10)
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: 	at com.android.webview.chromium.WebViewChromium.evaluateJavaScript(chromium-SystemWebViewGoogle6432.aab-stable-787112403:47)
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: 	at android.webkit.WebView.evaluateJavascript(WebView.java:895)
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: 	at com.wails.app.WailsJSBridge.lambda$sendCallback$1$com-wails-app-WailsJSBridge(WailsJSBridge.java:137)
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: 	at com.wails.app.WailsJSBridge$$ExternalSyntheticLambda0.run(D8$$SyntheticClass:0)
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: 	at android.os.Handler.handleCallback(Handler.java:1037)
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: 	at android.os.Handler.dispatchMessage(Handler.java:108)
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: 	at android.os.Looper.loopOnce(Looper.java:304)
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: 	at android.os.Looper.loop(Looper.java:430)
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: 	at android.app.ActivityThread.main(ActivityThread.java:9345)
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: 	at java.lang.reflect.Method.invoke(Native Method)
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: 	at com.android.internal.os.RuntimeInit$MethodAndArgsCaller.run(RuntimeInit.java:593)
07-31 16:24:43.157 10758 10758 W cr_AwContents: 	at com.android.internal.os.ZygoteInit.main(ZygoteInit.java:953)
```

### To Reproduce

In the app I am regularly polling updates from the go backend and I think the bug occured when such a request was in-flight while the View was being destroyed.

### Expected behaviour

It should not crash

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

I am not an expereinced Android native programmer, so I just asked Claude for a quick-fix and that worked for me:

In WailsJSBridge.java:

```
+    /**
+     * Marks this bridge's WebView as gone. Call before tearing down the
+     * WebView so callbacks from calls already running on {@link #executor}
+     * (e.g. a poll in flight when the Activity is destroyed) no-op instead of
+     * touching a destroyed WebView.
+     */
+    public void markDestroyed() {
+        destroyed = true;
+    }
+
     /**
      * Send a message to Go and return the response synchronously.
      * Called from JavaScript: wails.invoke(message)
@@ -134,7 +148,13 @@ public class WailsJSBridge {
             );
         }
 
-        webView.post(() -> webView.evaluateJavascript(js, null));
+        webView.post(() -> {
+            // Re-checked here, not just by callers before posting: destroy()
+            // can happen in the window between post() and this runnable
+            // actually executing on the UI thread.
+            if (destroyed) return;
+            webView.evaluateJavascript(js, null);
+        });
     }

```

In MainActivity.java:

```
@@ -57,6 +58,7 @@ public class MainActivity extends AppCompatActivity {
 
     private WebView webView;
     private WailsBridge bridge;
+    private WailsJSBridge jsBridge;
     // Battery: system-event receivers are registered only while the activity is
     // in the foreground (onStart) and torn down in onStop, so background battery/
     // network/screen broadcasts don't wake the app.
@@ -196,7 +198,8 @@ public class MainActivity extends AppCompatActivity {
         });
 
         // Add JavaScript interface for Go communication
-        webView.addJavascriptInterface(new WailsJSBridge(bridge, webView), "wails");
+        jsBridge = new WailsJSBridge(bridge, webView);
+        webView.addJavascriptInterface(jsBridge, "wails");
     }
 
     private void loadApplication() {
@@ -802,11 +805,26 @@ public class MainActivity extends AppCompatActivity {
     protected void onDestroy() {
         super.onDestroy();
         unregisterSystemEventReceivers();
+        // Mark the JS bridge destroyed before anything else below, so any
+        // invokeAsync call already running on its background executor - e.g.
+        // an in-flight AudioService.Progress() poll - finds the flag set and
+        // skips its evaluateJavascript callback instead of racing destroy().
+        if (jsBridge != null) {
+            jsBridge.markDestroyed();
+        }
         if (bridge != null) {
             bridge.shutdown();
         }
         if (webView != null) {
+            // WebView.destroy() while still attached to the view hierarchy
+            // logs "WebView.destroy() called while WebView is still attached
+            // to window" - detach it first.
+            ViewGroup parent = (ViewGroup) webView.getParent();
+            if (parent != null) {
+                parent.removeView(webView);
+            }
             webView.destroy();
+            webView = null;
         }
     }

```

But like I said, this is just a quick-and-dirty AI fix that worked for my specific issue, maybe you should look into it in more detail.

items.title: [v3]`wails3 generate appimage` looks for GTK3 runtime files on the new GTK4 default (alpha.93)
items.body:
### Description

Since alpha.93, the default CGO build target on Linux is GTK4 / WebKitGTK 6 (the GTK3 path is retained behind `-tags gtk3`, per the alpha.93 changelog). But `wails3 generate appimage` still hard-codes the WebKit2GTK 4.x runtime filenames when packaging, so on a runner that only has the GTK4 toolchain installed, AppImage generation aborts:

```
Processing GTK files. [3/5] 60% | 1m13s
ERROR  Unable to locate all required files: libwebkit2gtkinjectedbundle.so
task: Failed to run task "linux:create:appimage": exit status 1
```

The hardcoded list:

https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/v3.0.0-alpha.93/v3/internal/commands/appimage.go#L142

```go
filesNeeded := []string{"WebKitWebProcess", "WebKitNetworkProcess", "libwebkit2gtkinjectedbundle.so"}
```

No branching on build tag, so even when the binary it's packaging is linked against WebKitGTK 6, the bundler still goes looking for the GTK3 set.

### To Reproduce

1. `go.mod` pinned to `github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3 v3.0.0-alpha.93`, no `-tags gtk3`.
2. On Ubuntu 24.04: `sudo apt install libgtk-4-dev libwebkitgtk-6.0-dev` (no GTK3 dev packages).
3. `go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/cmd/wails3@v3.0.0-alpha.93` — succeeds.
4. `go build ./...` — succeeds, links against GTK4 / WebKitGTK 6.
5. `wails3 generate appimage -binary <APP> -icon <ICON> -desktopfile <FILE> -outputdir <DIR> -builddir <DIR>` — fails as above.

### Expected behaviour

When the binary is built against GTK4 / WebKitGTK 6, the AppImage bundler should pick the matching WebKitGTK 6 runtime files instead of the WebKit2GTK 4.x set — either by checking the build tag, ldd'ing the input binary, or taking a CLI flag.

### Attempted Fixes

Workaround that works today: pin the app build to `-tags gtk3` and put `libgtk-3-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` back on the runner. The changelog calls this the "legacy" path, but pre-alpha.93 it was just "the path", so the takeaway from a downstream perspective is "GTK4 AppImage isn't wired up yet" rather than "GTK3 was deprecated and you missed it".

### Additional context

Hit this when bumping a downstream project from alpha.90 → alpha.93. Same `Taskfile.yml` worked at alpha.90 with `libgtk-3-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` installed; failed at alpha.93 with the GTK4 packages; recovered at alpha.93 with `-tags gtk3` + GTK3 packages. Happy to attach `wails doctor` output from a matching Linux env if useful.

items.title: Webview custom scheme never cancels r.Context() when the client aborts a request (v2 and v3)

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
### Wails version family

v2

### Exact Wails version

2.13.0

### Operating System

Linux

### Description

When the frontend aborts an in-flight request (`xhr.abort()`, `AbortController`, navigation, window close), the `*http.Request` context on the Go side never cancels. Handlers keep running to completion.

This works correctly through the dev server, because that is a real `net/http` connection. It fails only through the `wails://` custom scheme bridge.

**This is present in both v2 and v3 on current `master`.**

## v2 (current `master`)

`v2/pkg/assetserver/assetserver_webview.go:109` uses plain `http.NewRequest`, which attaches `context.Background()`, and nothing downstream replaces it with anything tied to the real request lifecycle.

`v2/internal/frontend/desktop/darwin/WailsContext.m:499` implements `stopURLSchemeTask`, WebKit's abort callback, but it only closes the HTTP body input stream. It never signals Go.

## v3 (current `master`)

`v3/internal/assetserver/assetserver_webview.go:128`:

    ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
    defer cancel()

    req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, method, uri, body)

The context is cancellable, but `cancel` is only reachable via `defer`, so it fires when `processWebViewRequestInternal` returns - after `a.ServeHTTP(rw, req)` has already finished. Nothing connects it to the webview aborting the request, so `req.Context().Done()` cannot fire while a handler is still running.

Per platform on v3:

- **macOS** - `webView:stopURLSchemeTask:` is implemented at `v3/pkg/application/webview_window_darwin.m:653`, but again only closes the body stream. It never signals Go, so the `cancel` above is never called early.
- **Linux** - there is no abort signal observed at all. `GCancellable` / `g_cancellable` have zero occurrences anywhere under `v3/`.

## Consequence

Any handler that relies on `r.Context()` for cancellation cannot be cancelled from the UI. In my case (a desktop app that streams uploads to remote storage), closing the window mid-upload left the upload writing to remote storage and holding capacity reservations until the process itself exited. The user-visible symptom is work that continues after the window is gone.

The general shape: long-running or streaming handlers have no way to observe that the client has gone away, so they consume bandwidth, quota, or locks with nothing left to receive the result.

### To Reproduce

1. Register a handler that logs when its request context ends:

```go
func handler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    select {
    case <-r.Context().Done():
        log.Println("cancelled:", r.Context().Err())
    case <-time.After(30 * time.Second):
        log.Println("ran to completion, never cancelled")
    }
}
```

2. Call it from the frontend and abort after ~1s:

```js
const c = new AbortController()
fetch('/slow', { signal: c.signal }).catch(() => {})
setTimeout(() => c.abort(), 1000)
```

3. Observe the Go log output.

4. For comparison, run the same code through the dev server (`wails dev`, opened over real HTTP) and repeat - the cancellation is logged as expected there.

### Expected behaviour

`r.Context().Done()` should fire when the webview aborts the request, so the handler observes `context canceled` and can stop work.

Expected: `cancelled: context canceled` after ~1s.
Actual: `ran to completion, never cancelled` after 30s.

The dev server (real HTTP) already behaves as expected. Only the `wails://` custom scheme bridge does not.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

**Prior art in this repo.** PR #3632 attempted to fix this for macOS on v2 in July 2024, prompted by the same underlying problem (cancelling a request from the UI when using a chi router). In that thread @leaanthony sketched the preferred approach - pass the URL string from obj-c back to Go in `stopURLSchemeTask` and cancel the matching request there. @almas-x noted in review that the request key should include `r.Method()`, not just `r.URL()`. The PR was labelled `awaiting feedback` and closed unmerged in August 2025 for lack of author response. The code it targeted is unchanged today, and it never covered Linux.

I am not proposing a design here, since one was already discussed in that thread. One thing that may still be worth deciding: what Linux should do, since unlike macOS there is currently no abort signal being observed at all - that side looks like more than wiring up an existing callback.

**Workaround I ended up using.** Bind an ordinary `net/http` server to `127.0.0.1:0` and point the window at that real `http://` origin instead of the custom scheme. Cancellation then works because the window is a normal HTTP client.

On v3 this is supported directly via `WebviewWindowOptions.URL`. On v2 there is no public way to set the start URL, though the frontends already read a `starturl` context key internally - so on v2 this currently requires a small fork.

items.title: GTK4 window state events are not emitted and Size reports defaults

milestone.title: v3.0.0-beta.0
milestone.description: Internal Beta staging milestone. Scope: release-branch synchronization, automated hardening fixes, compatibility contract, release dashboard/record, and reproducible local evidence. Not published: the release tool increments this staging version to beta.1.

items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Operating System

Linux

### Description

The default GTK4 backend does not emit the common maximise, unmaximise, minimise, unminimise, fullscreen, and unfullscreen window events when the native toplevel state changes.

The current GTK4 callback watches `GtkWindow` maximized/fullscreened properties but only emits `WindowDidResize`, and only while the window is maximised or fullscreen. Minimise transitions are not observed. In addition, `Window.Size()` prefers `gtk_window_get_default_size()`, so after a user resize it can keep returning the configured default instead of the live surface size.

Together these behaviours prevent applications from reliably tracking the normal window size and maximised state.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a Wails v3 application using the default GTK4 Linux backend.
2. Register handlers for `WindowMaximise`, `WindowUnMaximise`, `WindowMinimise`, `WindowUnMinimise`, `WindowFullscreen`, `WindowUnFullscreen`, and `WindowDidResize`.
3. Run the application with `wails3 dev`.
4. Resize, maximise, restore, minimise, restore, and toggle fullscreen.
5. Query `Window.Size()` after a normal resize.

The common state events are not emitted consistently, and the queried size may remain the configured default.

### Expected behaviour

GTK4 should emit the same common state-transition events as the other platform backends. `WindowDidResize` should follow live `GdkSurface` size changes, and `Window.Size()` should return the live widget size after realization.

### Attempted Fixes

The GTK4 backend can subscribe to `notify::width`, `notify::height`, and `notify::state` on the realised toplevel `GdkSurface`. Diffing consecutive `GdkToplevelState` snapshots provides the corresponding common edge events while keeping initial maximised/fullscreen state observable.

### System Details

- Fedora Kinoite 44
- Linux amd64
- Go 1.26.5
- GTK 4.22.4
- WebKitGTK 2.52.5 (6.0 API)

`wails3 doctor` could not run in the current Nix-provided test environment because its runtime library path mixed incompatible system and Nix glibc versions. The affected package and its new transition tests compile and pass with the GTK4/WebKitGTK 6.0 development environment.

### Additional context

A fix with unit coverage is ready in `savely-krasovsky:fix/gtk4-window-state-events`.

items.title: Linux: repeated SIGABRT/SIGSEGV in WebKitGTK/JSC main loop on v3.0.0-alpha2.103
items.body:
### Description

We are seeing repeated native crashes on Linux after upgrading to Wails `v3.0.0-alpha2.103`.

This is a long-running Wails desktop application on Linux using WebKitGTK. The app updates the UI frequently and loads local media/resources through the WebView. After the process crashes, an external watchdog restarts it.

We previously reported related Linux issues in:

- https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/issues/5557
- https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/issues/5552

After upgrading to `v3.0.0-alpha2.103` and removing local Wails source patches, the crashes still happen.

### Environment

- Wails: `v3.0.0-alpha2.103`
- Go: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`
- GTK: `3.24.41`
- WebKitGTK: `2.50.4`
- GLib: `2.80.1`
- OS: Linux x86_64

### Crash frequency

After deployment, the watchdog recorded 10 crashes within about 15 hours.

All exits were:

```text
signal: aborted (core dumped)
```

### Main crash signature

9 out of 10 crashes have the same signature.

stderr:

```text
SIGSEGV: segmentation violation
PC=0x... sigcode=1 addr=0x28
signal arrived during cgo execution

goroutine 1 [syscall, locked to thread]:
runtime.cgocall(...)
github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application._Cfunc_g_application_run(...)
github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application.appRun(...)
    github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3@v3.0.0-alpha2.103/pkg/application/linux_cgo_gtk3.go:639
github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application.(*linuxApp).run(...)
github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application.(*App).Run(...)
main.main()
```

Native coredump stack example:

```text
Signal: 6 (ABRT)

#9  libjavascriptcoregtk-4.1.so.0 + 0x1950c99
#11 libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0 + 0x99295e
#12 libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0 + 0x30f9791
#13 libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0 + 0xde82cd
#14 libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0 + 0xde83fd
#15 libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0 + 0xe3e701
#16 g_object_unref
#17 libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0 + 0xe3e285
#18 libgio-2.0.so.0
#23 g_main_context_iteration
#24 g_application_run
```

At startup we also consistently see:

```text
GLib-GObject-CRITICAL **: g_value_set_boxed: assertion 'G_VALUE_HOLDS_BOXED (value)' failed
dbind-WARNING **: AT-SPI: Error retrieving accessibility bus address
Overriding existing handler for signal 10. Set JSC_SIGNAL_FOR_GC if you want WebKit to use a different signal
```

### One different crash

One crash happened immediately after restart, before the WebKit child process was fully running:

```text
runtime: bad pointer in frame github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application.(*linuxWebviewWindow).setupSignalHandlers at 0xc000034aa8: 0x1
fatal error: invalid pointer found on stack
```

This also occurred on `v3.0.0-alpha2.103`.

### Diagnostics before crashes

Runtime diagnostics before the crashes do not suggest resource exhaustion:

- No OOM events in kernel logs
- Goroutines stable, usually around `32-37`
- File descriptors stable, around `58-59`
- Main process threads stable, around `31-53`
- Child processes stable:
  - 2 helper child processes
  - 1 WebKitNetworkProcess
  - 1 WebKitWebProcess
- No Go panic from application business logic before the native crash

Example diagnostic snapshot before one crash:

```text
goroutines: 32
main process threads: 33
fdCount: 58
main RSS: ~313 MB
child processes: 4
webkit processes: 2
```

### Notes

Frontend WebAudio is not used for the task-arrival notification path anymore. Notification sound is handled outside the WebView path. The crash still occurs after this change.

The WebView still performs frequent UI updates and local resource/media rendering.

### Questions

1. Could this still be related to the fixes for #5557 or #5552, or is this a different WebKitGTK/JSC crash path?
2. Is the `Overriding existing handler for signal 10. Set JSC_SIGNAL_FOR_GC...` warning expected in Wails v3 on Linux?
3. Could Wails' `setupSignalHandlers` or WebKit/JSC signal handling be conflicting with Go runtime signal handling?
4. Is there a recommended runtime setting for Wails v3 Linux apps to avoid this WebKitGTK/JSC crash path?
5. Would setting `JSC_SIGNAL_FOR_GC` be recommended or harmful for Wails apps?
6. Are there known unsafe patterns around WebKit resource release / request handling / local asset serving that could trigger this `g_object_unref` crash?

### Expected behavior

The Wails app should keep running for long periods under normal UI updates.

### Actual behavior

The app repeatedly aborts with native WebKitGTK/JSC crashes inside the GTK main loop.

Release-branch audit completed against `3e03d19bdc5599c7eac71185f89c6e0596dec1de`. Corrections remain open. This issue is the authoritative follow-up tracker; the local report records audit evidence.

# Wails v3 release documentation audit

An audit of the checked-in v3 documentation found **31 actionable findings: 3 P1, 25 P2 and 3 P3**. The highest priorities are unsafe security examples and a misleading claim that binding directives prevent frontend access. The site builds and its links validate, but several documented examples and workflows do not match the implementation.

## Scope and baseline

- Audit date: 25 October 2026. Authoritative tracker: [Wails #6337](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/issues/6337), following the completed #5430 and #6086 accuracy passes. This report records evidence; follow-up work and status belong on GitHub.
- Audited source: `wailsapp/wails`, branch `releases/v3.0.0`, commit `3e03d19bdc5599c7eac71185f89c6e0596dec1de`; audit branch `codex/v3-release-docs-audit`.
- Source of truth: `docs/mpress/content/`, the v3 module, CLI parser, binding generator, runtime, standard templates, build assets and repository workflows. The Docusaurus website is the v2 site and was excluded.
- Inventory: 204 English pages, 52,259 English source lines, nine translated sets (1,827 translated pages; the new release-policy page has no locale copies), and the supporting contributor/build references. Historical blog posts and changelog entries were inventoried but were not treated as current API promises.
- The English page inventory and site were checked on this release branch. Identifier/source sweeps from the initial audit were reconciled with the changed release-branch files. Semantic review concentrated on onboarding, API references, binding generation, events/lifecycle, build/platform instructions, security, testing and contribution guidance. Streams, updater, mobile, menus, dialogs and environment material received targeted source checks, not exhaustive platform execution.
- This is an audit report, not a correction patch. Production documentation and implementation were left unchanged. Findings were verified against the release checkout and its code; the live-site deployment was not audited.

## Severity and evidence

P1 means copied guidance can compromise application security. P2 means a documented workflow, API contract or validation gate is materially wrong or blocked. P3 means a narrower inconsistency or misleading destination. Counts are distinct remediation items; repeated instances and translation diagnostics are not counted as separate defects.

Validation labels distinguish executed reproductions from source inspection. Native macOS/Windows UI, Linux distribution installs, code signing and mobile device workflows were not executed.

## Findings

### F01 P1 Encryption example reuses the GCM nonce

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/security.md:113`.

The example allocates a zero-filled nonce for every call and immediately passes it to `gcm.Seal`. It never fills the nonce with randomness. Executing the example twice with the same key and plaintext produced identical ciphertext and the nonce `000000000000000000000000`.

**Impact:** Applications copying this security example reuse a GCM nonce under the same key, compromising the security properties of authenticated encryption. This is a defect in the example; this audit does not establish that Wails itself uses this helper.

**Correction:** Replace it with a complete standard-library example using a fresh nonce from `crypto/rand`, or an appropriate random-nonce AEAD API. Explain the nonce prefix and matching decryption. [Go cipher reference](https://pkg.go.dev/crypto/cipher#NewGCM) documents the nonce requirement.

**Validation:** Executed standalone Go reproduction.

### F02 P1 File access example does not confine reads to the allowed directory

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/security.md:169`.

`strings.HasPrefix(absPath, allowedDir)` accepts a sibling directory sharing the prefix. The same code follows symlinks out of the allowed directory. A temporary fixture returned an outside file through both `allowed-outside/secret` and `allowed/link`, with no error.

**Impact:** Readers may expose files outside the intended directory through a bound method copied from the security guide.

**Correction:** Use a filesystem API that confines resolution beneath a root, such as `os.OpenRoot` and root-relative operations, and document supported Go versions. A lexical relative-path check alone does not address symlink escape.

**Validation:** Executed both sibling-prefix and symlink reproductions.

### F03 P1 Binding directives are presented as preventing frontend exposure

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/advanced.md:47`; `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/advanced.md:59`; `docs/mpress/content/contributing/architecture/bindings.md:88`.

`internal/generator/collect/service.go:239` makes `ignore` omit a generated method and makes `internal` suppress its JS export. The generated directives fixture still contains a callable `InternalMethod`. Runtime registration in `pkg/application/bindings.go:134` reflects exported Go methods and does not read source comments. A server-tagged probe registered both annotated methods and retrieved both by their fully qualified binding names.

**Impact:** A developer can mistake removal from the generated SDK for an access-control boundary and leave privileged exported methods callable.

**Correction:** Describe both directives as code-generation controls. State that exported methods remain registered in normal builds and that private operations must be unexported or moved off the bound service; enforce authorisation inside exposed operations. Qualify any separate obfuscation behaviour rather than promising universal hiding.

**Validation:** Executed binding registry probe with both directives.

### F04 P2 Typed event factories and signatures disagree with generated string constants

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/reference/frontend-runtime.md:130`; `docs/mpress/content/reference/frontend-runtime.md:161`; `docs/mpress/content/reference/frontend-runtime.md:225`.

The reference imports `UserUpdated`/`UserLogin` from `./bindings/events`, invokes them as factories, and describes `EventType<T>` overloads. This release branch **does generate** `events/index.ts`: `internal/generator/render/eventnames.go` and `eventnames.js.tmpl` export string constants. Consequently `Events.On(UserLogin, handler)` and the import path can be valid, but `UserUpdated(payload)` is not callable. The runtime uses `CustomEvents` augmentation and event-name strings.

**Impact:** Factory-style calls and documented overload signatures remain wrong; claiming that the events module is absent would itself be wrong on this release branch. Existing report [#5645](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/issues/5645) covers the original typed-event discovery problem.

**Correction:** Retain the generated constants and use `Events.Emit(UserUpdated, payload)`, or the string-literal equivalent. Document the runtime's actual name-based generics rather than EventType factories, and validate the example with this generator.

**Validation:** Compared release runtime signatures and generator templates; ran the release event-name renderer test and generated an events fixture.

### F05 P2 Typed events plugin example omits its required bindings path

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/reference/frontend-runtime.md:93`.

The reference configures `plugins: [wails()]`. `src/plugins/vite.ts:25` requires `bindingsRoot: string`, then resolves `${bindingsRoot}/github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/internal/eventcreate`. Without the argument it attempts a path starting with `undefined/`. The built-in Vanilla config correctly passes `wails("./bindings")`.

**Impact:** The documented plugin configuration fails type checking or event-module resolution.

**Correction:** Pass the bindings directory and explain that it is relative to the Vite project. Align with `guides/dev/frontend-frameworks.md:84` and the built-in template.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F06 P2 Time mappings contradict one another and omit the controlling option

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/models.md:319`; `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/models.md:468`; `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/models.md:710`; `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/methods.md:334`; `docs/mpress/content/concepts/bridge.md:131`.

The tables say `time.Time` becomes `any`; other sections promise `Date` and call `.getTime()`. `internal/flags/bindings.go:16` exposes `-time-type` with default `string`. The generated build task passes `-time-type=Date` for class/JS templates, but omits it for TypeScript interface templates. Committed fixtures demonstrate `Time: string` in the interface configuration and `Time: Date` with `DateFromTime` conversion in the class configuration.

**Impact:** Date methods fail for the default interface/string path. Switching generation modes silently changes the expected data shape if the reader follows these pages.

**Correction:** Document string versus Date explicitly, including `-time-type`, template defaults, JSON wire representation, and construction behaviour. Generate examples for both modes; do not replace every mapping with one universal type.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F07 P2 Model quick start reads a property excluded by its own JSON tag

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/models.md:21`; `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/models.md:42`.

The Go example declares `Name string` with `json:"name"`, then JavaScript reads `user.Name`. The later generated-model example on the same page uses `name` correctly.

**Impact:** The very first example returns `undefined` rather than the user name.

**Correction:** Read `user.name` and use one generated fixture to keep the Go definition and frontend property accesses aligned.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F08 P2 Counter service example does not compile

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/methods.md:100`.

The stateful counter declares `mu sync.Mutex`, then `GetCount` calls `RLock` and `RUnlock`, methods of `sync.RWMutex`, not `sync.Mutex`.

**Impact:** Copying this complete service fails compilation.

**Correction:** Use `sync.RWMutex`, as the services page already does, or use `Lock`/`Unlock` consistently.

**Validation:** Extracted the complete CounterService example and compiled it with Go; RLock and RUnlock were both rejected on sync.Mutex.

### F09 P2 Custom service names are said to allow multiple instances of one type

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/services.md:292`; `docs/mpress/content/features/bindings/services.md:307`.

The listed use cases for `ServiceOptions.Name` include multiple instances of the same service type. `pkg/application/services.go:22` limits the name to logging/debugging. `Bindings.Add` rejects a duplicate fully qualified method regardless of that display name, explicitly saying to wrap additional instances in dedicated structs.

**Impact:** The suggested registration pattern fails rather than exposing two independently named service instances.

**Correction:** Remove that use case and demonstrate distinct wrapper types. Explain that `Name` does not change a binding namespace.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F10 P2 Window creation callback is incorrectly described as runtime ready

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/features/windows/events.md:52`.

`WindowManager.addAndRun` calls the OnCreate callbacks before `runOrDeferToAppRun`. Before `app.Run`, no window runtime has started. The page separately documents `WindowRuntimeReady` as the safe point for JavaScript.

**Impact:** Readers may emit events or call JavaScript too early and lose startup messages.

**Correction:** Describe OnCreate as a configuration/registration callback. Use `WindowRuntimeReady` for operations requiring the frontend runtime.

**Validation:** Traced the exact manager call order.

### F11 P2 Server mode reference gives incorrect return behaviour

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/server-build.md:202`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/server-build.md:212`.

The page says `NewWithOptions` warns and returns nil, and `app.Screen.GetPrimary()` returns an error. The shared manager creates a non-nil `WebviewWindow`; GetPrimary has signature `*Screen` and returns nil when there is no primary screen. A server-tagged probe observed `window nil=false` and `primary nil=true`.

**Impact:** Server adaptations based on the documented nil/error checks will be wrong; blindly dereferencing the screen can panic.

**Correction:** Separate native-host availability from Go window objects. Document exact Go signatures, nil behaviour, and the browser-side errors separately.

**Validation:** Executed a server-tagged manager probe.

### F12 P2 Build guides disagree about whether an ordinary build is debug or production

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/getting-started/your-first-app.md:83`; `docs/mpress/content/getting-started/your-first-app.md:112`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/cli.md:83`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/build/cross-platform.md:21`.

The first-app and CLI guide promise a debug executable and console logging from `wails3 build`. The cross-platform guide correctly calls it production by default. Current Linux/macOS/Windows build assets choose production flags unless `DEV=true` is supplied.

**Impact:** Users cannot follow the promised debugging workflow and may assume inspector/logging behaviour that was compiled out.

**Correction:** Document production as the generated default. Explain `wails3 dev` and any supported explicit DEV override separately, including platform inspector constraints.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F13 P2 Several build examples pass variables the generated tasks do not use

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/cli.md:98`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/cli.md:163`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/cli.md:213`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/build/customization.md:125`.

Examples use `PLATFORM=linux CONFIG=production` and `PLATFORM=windows ARCH=amd64`. The wrapper selects `GOOS`; the generated root task dispatches on `.GOOS`; platform tasks select development flags using `.DEV`. PLATFORM and CONFIG do not control the stock tasks.

**Impact:** A command can succeed while building the host platform or an unintended mode.

**Correction:** Use `GOOS=...` and the supported mode variable, and label invented variables as examples for custom Taskfiles rather than built-in controls.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F14 P2 macOS deployment promise disagrees with the generated build target

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/getting-started/installation.md:11`.

Installation advertises Intel deployment to 10.13 and Apple Silicon 11.0. `build_assets/darwin/Taskfile.yml:54` sets C flags, linker flags and `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` to 12.0. Some package-level Cgo directives still name 10.13, so even the source has multiple apparent minima.

**Impact:** The documented support promise does not describe binaries produced by the standard build workflow.

**Correction:** Establish one tested deployment contract, distinguish development-host requirements from binary runtime minimums, and align native and Docker builds. Do not infer a new framework-wide minimum solely from one flag.

**Validation:** Static build-setting contradiction; older macOS execution not tested.

### F15 P2 Linux missing-dependency remedy installs the legacy stack for the default build

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/build/linux.md:184`.

The guide correctly says GTK4/WebKitGTK 6.0 is the default, then its unqualified missing-WebKit remedy installs WebKit2GTK 4.1 runtime packages. Those packages match the legacy `gtk3` build, not the default stack.

**Impact:** A user with a default binary follows the troubleshooting instructions and still lacks its runtime library.

**Correction:** Provide separate GTK4/WebKitGTK 6.0 and legacy GTK3/WebKit2GTK 4.1 remedies, tied to the actual build tag and target distribution. Qualify AppImage portability claims by bundled/external runtime requirements.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F16 P2 Custom transport walkthrough omits a required interface method

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/custom-transport.md:43`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/custom-transport.md:73`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/custom-transport.md:120`.

The walkthrough implements Start and Stop and assigns `&MyCustomTransport{}` to Options.Transport. It never implements `JSClient() []byte`, although the reference later on the same page and `pkg/application/transport.go:18` both require it.

### F17 P2 End to end guide points a backend workflow at a frontend-only server

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/e2e-testing.md:33`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/e2e-testing.md:136`.

The guide uses Playwright against port 9245, the Vite UI preview. Wails native invocation is not provided by an ordinary browser tab there. The CI example starts neither Vite nor a Wails server and supplies no mocks or `webServer` configuration. `guides/build/customization.md:239` explicitly warns that bindings do not work at that browser-preview URL.

**Impact:** The claimed complete workflow has no backend connection locally and no running app in CI.

**Correction:** Choose and document a real harness: explicit mocks for UI-only tests, server-tag integration tests for bindings, or a supported native-webview automation path. Start and wait for that harness in CI; state which native capabilities it excludes.

**Validation:** Source comparison.

### F18 P2 End to end examples confuse browser upload and viewport APIs with native UI

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/e2e-testing.md:80`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/e2e-testing.md:100`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/e2e-testing.md:63`.

The save-dialog example handles a Playwright `filechooser` and calls `setFiles`, which is an HTML file-upload operation, not a native save dialog. The window test checks a newly created browser viewport without setting it to 800x600, not a Wails window. The delete test registers its browser dialog handler after the triggering click.

**Impact:** Tests either fail, dismiss the confirmation before handling it, or assert properties unrelated to the native behaviour they claim to validate.

**Correction:** Use uploads only for HTML inputs, register browser-dialog handlers before the action, and distinguish browser viewport assertions from native window checks. [Playwright upload documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/input#upload-files) and [dialog documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/dialogs) define the supported operations.

**Validation:** Compared examples with Playwright primary documentation; no GUI automation executed.

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/build/windows.md:22`; `docs/mpress/content/reference/cli.md:108`.

### F21 P2 CLI reference invents a global flag spelling and scope

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/reference/cli.md:111`; `docs/mpress/content/guides/cli.md:660`.

### F22 P2 CLI reference denies a signing command that the binary exposes

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/reference/cli.md:71`.

The page explicitly says there is no `wails3 signing` command. The audited binary lists `signing` and `entitlements` at top level, and `wails3 signing --help` prints signing-specific flags. Conversely, `setup signing --help` prints setup help. This occurs despite the apparent nested construction in main.go.

**Impact:** The reference gives an absolute command-availability claim contradicted by the actual parser. Signing setup instructions need an executable check, not just inspection of builder calls.

### F24 P2 Release documentation is missing nine required translations

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/contributing/release-policy.md:1`; `docs/mpress/CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/mpress/scripts/check_translations.py`.

The release branch adds an English release-policy page, marked as a draft in its prose, without any of the nine locale copies. It has no build metadata excluding it from publication. The coverage checker reports nine missing translations. The site build includes the English route; its rendered-site validator requires corresponding translated routes. Stale segment findings are warnings unless --strict is supplied; missing translation files still fail the ordinary gate.

**Impact:** Warning-only stale auditing does not waive missing files. The release validation gate remains blocked by this specific page. The standalone M-Press build succeeds; `docs/mpress/scripts/build.sh` additionally runs the failing translation coverage check before invoking that build.

**Correction:** Translate the page when the owner approves its policy, or explicitly exclude an unpublished draft from both publication and coverage under one consistent rule. Do not silently accept missing published routes or treat draft policy as an approved release decision.

**Validation:** Ran the release coverage checker, which reports exactly nine missing files; rebuilt the site with M-Press 1.0.19. Full audit reports nine errors and 651 non-blocking warnings, with the same nine missing routes in the rendered-site check.

### F25 P2 Panic guide says a goroutine panic affects only that goroutine

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/guides/panic-handling.md:15`.

The guide says only the panicking goroutine is affected. A standalone unrecovered goroutine panic terminates the process; the probe exited with status 2. Recovery must occur in that same goroutine. Wails recovery around particular dispatch paths is a separate behaviour.

**Impact:** Readers may assume a background worker crash is isolated and omit necessary recovery at its boundary.

**Correction:** Describe stack unwinding and process termination accurately, then identify precisely which Wails callbacks are recovered. Preserve the existing advice to handle background goroutines explicitly.

**Validation:** Executed standalone background-panic reproduction.

### F31 P2 Installation routes disagree about the required Go toolchain

**Documentation:** `docs/mpress/content/getting-started/installation.md:25`; `docs/mpress/content/quick-start/installation.md:25`; `docs/mpress/content/status.md:24`.

The public release checkout has conflicting Go requirements: `getting-started/installation.md:25` says Go 1.24, while `quick-start/installation.md:25` and `status.md:24` say Go 1.25. ## Structural recommendations

The main maintenance problem is duplicated reference material drifting independently. There are two installation/first-app routes, two CLI references, several event and menu references, and repeated Go-to-JavaScript mapping tables. The CLI still opens the older getting-started route. Consolidate factual reference contracts into one maintained source, and let tutorials link to those facts.

Under Diataxis, keep the first-app and QR/TODO/Notes pages as tutorials with one reproducible path and exact generated filenames. Keep field types, default values, CLI flags and conversion rules in reference pages derived from executable fixtures. Keep how-to guides such as custom transport, signing and end-to-end testing complete enough to achieve their stated outcome. Explanation pages can discuss alternatives without duplicating normative API tables.

Fix the three P1 items first, then the first-app/event/type examples and build contracts, then testing and contribution gates. Avoid a broad rewrite until examples can be regenerated and checked. For upstream triage, these corrections are bugs: prioritise by severity and keep fixes outside the feature-only v3.1.0 milestone/project, following the repository release policy. The findings are tracked in Wails #6337; no PR or push was made. Existing reports were searched before filing; the completed #5430/#6086 and typed-event #5645 context is retained.

Executed probes used temporary files and directories, the checked-in v3 module and Go 1.26.5. CLI probes were built with the server tag to avoid requiring a desktop display; native signing and packaging actions were not invoked.

The binding probe used `application.NewBindings(nil, nil)`, added `application.NewService(&AuditService{})` after creating an App, and queried `Bindings.Get(&application.CallOptions{MethodName: name})` for both fully qualified method names. AuditService declared one exported method with each directive. The probe did not start a listening server or invoke privileged methods.

The release translation audit with M-Press 1.0.19 reports nine missing-file errors and 651 warnings: 252 missing-segment, 216 protected-content, 73 untranslated, 54 glossary, 36 structure, nine missing-file, nine invalid-target and two requirement-language findings. These are checker diagnostics, not 651 independently confirmed translation defects.

## Follow up boundaries

This report applies to the checked-in `releases/v3.0.0` baseline above. It makes no claim about the live website or a later branch tip. Native platform, device and signing workflows remain unexecuted where noted. The report contains evidence and suggested corrections; GitHub #6337 is the work tracker, and no documentation or implementation fixes are included in this commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- Correct or explicitly adjudicate each applicable finding against the release branch.
- Preserve generated event-name constants and correct factory-style usage (#5645).
- Replace unsafe copied examples and compile-check corrected examples.
- Reconcile release-policy translation coverage and the stated Go requirements.
- Run the pinned documentation checks and relevant executable examples; record platform limits.
- Keep bug fixes outside the feature-only v3.1.0 milestone/project and prioritise security guidance.

No documentation fixes, framework changes, PR, push or publication were performed by this audit. #5430 and #6086 remain completed historical passes.

items.body:
**Description**

When compiling Go applications using Wails with `go get/go build/go install`, a set of warnings are printed to the terminal. These warnings are mainly due to the use of two deprecated functions of Webkit, namely `webkit_javascript_result_get_global_context` and `webkit_javascript_result_get_value`.

This is mostly apparent when using `go install ./...` to build all Go packages and commands of a given repository, as otherwise one would use `wails build` (which seems to silent these warnings).

For at least one of the deprecated functions (`webkit_javascript_result_get_value`), a replacement function is suggested (`webkit_javascript_result_get_js_value`).

```
‘webkit_javascript_result_get_value’ is deprecated: Use 'webkit_javascript_result_get_js_value' instead
```

```
warning: ‘webkit_javascript_result_get_global_context’ is deprecated
```

### Description

When `task linux:generate:dotdesktop` is called, the generated file changes the name in desktop entry to lower case and also removes all spaces. This affects how the app is named on the menu



### To Reproduce

For a quick test, try this

1.  Run `wails3 generate .desktop -name "My app" - exec "my-app"`
2.  Open the generated `my-app.desktop` .
`[Desktop Entry]
Type=Application
Name=my-app
Exec=my-app
Categories=
Terminal=false
Keywords=wails
Version=1.0
StartupNotify=false`






### Expected behaviour

The name should be as entered unless it is outside the [FreeDesktop specs](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry/latest/value-types.html) .

Expected output should be
`[Desktop Entry]
Type=Application
Name=My App
Exec=my-app
Categories=
Terminal=false
